title: Four Swedish lake samples gave no clear link between annual temperature change and phytoplankton turnover in 1996-2022
abstract: We tested whether larger annual air temperature changes went with larger year-to-year changes in phytoplankton composition. Four region and period models used 2,611 consecutive-year pairs at 110 Swedish lakes in 1996-2022. Models controlled lake and year effects and changes in rain, colour, phosphorus and pH. Temperature slopes were -0.012, -0.014, -0.042 and -0.045 Hellinger distance units per C. All four adjusted intervals included zero. Combining labels by first name, adding signed temperature change or lake trends, and using stable panels gave the same limited null result. Year controls removed much of the weather contrast. Wide intervals, annual weather that includes months after August sampling, and missing count effort and analyst records limit inference. This study tests no causal climate or air pollution effect. The package gives code, a derived pair panel, exact source hashes, results and a figure.

display.caption: Temperature-change slopes for community distance, with four-test adjusted intervals. First-name groups test sensitivity to taxon detail. All intervals include zero.
